evidence.excerpt: title: Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense; submitted: 2026-10-29; categories: cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.RO; authors: Khawaja Abaid Ullah; Ananya Acharya; Mohammad Javad Khojasteh; abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multi-agent teams raises a fundamental architectural question: whether task allocation should be centralized in a single LLM controller or distributed across autonomous LLM agents, particularly when communication is unreliable. In a deliberately simplified perimeter-defense simulation against LLM-controlled intruders, we compared a central commander, an auction-based consensus team and independent agents under five network conditions. Breach rates were 15% for the consensus team, 32% for the commander and 29% for independent agents, and of the different network conditions, only limited radio range changed a team's breach rate, raising the commander's. In consensus team, giving a low-cost LLM more authority over the bid computation raised breaches by 38 percentage points.
